items.title: Delfeayo Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: at the time they had, of course, Branford and Wynton, my dad, Donald [Harrison] and Terence [Blanchard].

ctx.x: Yeah, RCA Novus was the – the funny thing about – I was a long time between recordings. What happened was, CBS offered me the same contract as RCA Novus, with a signing bonus, a nice signing bonus, but I felt that CBS had a tendency to have artists on their roster that they didn’t support very much. So my thinking was, by going to RCA Novus, I’d have a better chance of receiving support than – if I went to CBS, at the time they had, of course, Branford and Wynton, my dad, Donald [Harrison] and Terence…

would be six years after that I made Musashi with King Records, right? 1990, 1991? Right. Five or six years after that, I was approached by King Records. They said, why aren’t you recording? I said, this is the situation. They said okay, and I went to Japan, recorded with Japanese musicians. Miyamoto Musashi is a person that Elvin’s wife Keiko would always talk about. Elvin would talk about The Book of Five Rings. I spent a substantial amount of time in Japan with Elvin. I just figured, for the next record I’d…
